nodes.t: A map of the whole US that shows where wild clay is likely to be. Tap any spot to see the soil there, how deep the clay sits, its raw colour and how promising it is, with the reasons. Everything else in this diagram is how people come across it, how I keep track of what works, and getting it onto phones.
The places I share clay finds. Each post gets people curious, and the link in it brings them to the map, so I can see which places send people.

Notes on wild clay for every state: the soils the map rates there, where they sit and how promising each one is, with every fact traced to where it came from. The posts here are made from these notes.
Short videos on my account, wildclayhunt, from my own digs. I’m still working out how they’re made.

My Pinterest, wildclayhunt, where I share wild clay and the places it turns up. From Nov 9 a pin goes out every weekday through June: Virginia one county at a time, and 64 towns across the country known for their clay. Each one opens the map right at its spot.
Are.na is a site for collecting and connecting ideas. The Georgeville notes are laid out there as a collection, with a link to the map.
The Wild Clay Hunt, my weekly email newsletter about finding clay. Nine issues so far.
A page for each of the 1,239 soil types the map rates, plus a page per state and a guide to finding wild clay, so someone searching for clay near them can land on the map.
How I keep track of what works: a few numbers, checked once a week. They help me pick which clay to write about next.

Who came, how many looked up a spot, how many upgraded to Pro (the paid version) and where they came from. The 30 days to Nov 9: 302 visitors, 95 looked something up, 7 upgraded, my testers among them. Launch week alone: 151 came and 59 looked something up, against 39 and 22 the week before.

How many people came through each place’s link, so I can see which places send people. Bots and my own visits are left out. The first week: Instagram 28, Substack 1. Pinterest’s first pin goes out Nov 9.

The same count for app downloads, from each store’s own figures. The App Store’s comes first, once enough people have downloaded the app through a place’s link; Google Play’s once the Android app is public.
Getting the map onto phones as an app: store listings, screenshots, testers and the steps for release day.
On the App Store since Nov 6, 2026, with Pro as an in-app upgrade.
The Android version is being tried out by a small group of invited potters before it goes public.
The steps for going public, one store at a time.
steps: Nov 6 · The site and every place’s link send iPhones to the App Store.
Nov 6 · An Instagram story and a Substack note.
Nov 5 · A how-to, cut, with a stand-in voice until I record mine.
After the testing, once Google approves it.
